payload.summary: MaterialDNA capped dense-array validation rejects over-cap history/anomaly data only after scanning the entire supplied table, so the 32-entry contract does not currently bound validation work for oversized plain-data inputs.
failedInvariants: validateDenseArray(value, maxCount) should stop once more than maxCount valid array keys are observed rather than continue scanning an input already known invalid.
The history/anomaly cardinality caps should bound rejection work for oversized dense-array inputs as well as accepted canonical cardinality.
evidence: src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau currently increments entryCount inside the pairs loop but checks entryCount > maxCount only after that loop completes.
The helper gates history and anomaly marker arrays with MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES = 32 and MAX_ANOMALY_MARKERS = 32.

Merged PR #50 described these strict MaterialDNA bounds as preventing pathologically large state payloads from consuming unbounded validation resources; current scan ordering leaves rejection cost proportional to supplied key count.
The current MaterialDNA counter salvage is isolated in HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-COUNTERS / PR #353; the new follow-on lane depends on it to avoid same-file overlap.
